questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word: **CAUSTIC**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Sarcastic**.

• **Example:** Her caustic comments about his work left him feeling insulted.
 
 
• **"Sarcastic"** refers to using irony to mock or convey contempt. (व्यंग्यात्मक)
 
 
• **Example:** He made a sarcastic remark about her punctuality, knowing she was always late.
 
 
• Hence, the word "caustic" aligns closely with "sarcastic" in terms of its meaning.

• **Example:** The weather today is mild, perfect for a picnic.
 
 

 
• **Gentle** (कोमल): Having or showing a mild, kind, or tender temperament.
 
 
• **Example:** He gave her a gentle push to signal that it was her turn to speak.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The reforms being recommended by the panel (1)/ are not only intended to streamline administrative functions (2)/ but also addressing the asymmetries in resource allocation (3)/ that have long plagued rural districts. (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence is in part **(3)**, where the phrase "**but also addressing**" is incorrect.
 
• The phrase should maintain parallelism with the earlier phrase "**to streamline**." Thus, "**addressing**" should be replaced with "**to address**."
 
• Parallel structure ensures grammatical consistency and improves readability.
 
• Therefore, the corrected phrase will be "**but also to address the asymmetries in resource allocation**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The reforms being recommended by the panel are not only intended to streamline administrative functions but also to address the asymmetries in resource allocation that have long plagued rural districts."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **(1): "The reforms being recommended by the panel"** – This part is grammatically correct and requires no changes.
 
• **(2): "are not only intended to streamline administrative functions"** – This part is also correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **(4): "that have long plagued rural districts"** – This part is grammatically correct and needs no changes.

questions.question:
**Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:**

What the committee failed to deliberate on adequately (1)/ were not the policy's objectives themselves, (2)/ but the political ramifications it (3)/ might have had if implemented without broader consensus. (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the phrase **"were not the policy's objectives themselves" **present in part 2 of the sentence.
 
• The verb "**were**" is incorrectly used as the subject "**What the committee failed to deliberate on adequately**" is singular and requires a singular verb.
 
• The correct verb should be **"was"** instead of "were."
 
• This ensures subject-verb agreement, which is essential for grammatical correctness.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"What the committee failed to deliberate on adequately **was not the policy's objectives themselves,** but the political ramifications it might have had if implemented without broader consensus."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part 1:** "What the committee failed to deliberate on adequately" – This part is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Part 3:** "but the political ramifications it" – This part is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Part 4:** "might have had if implemented without broader consensus" – This part is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **No error** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 2.
</ul

questions.question:
**Change the following from active to passive:**

The laboratory will have double-checked the reagents by dawn.

options.text: The reagents have been double-checked by the laboratory by dawn.
The reagents will have been double-checked by the laboratory by dawn.
The reagents will be double-checked by the laboratory by dawn.
The reagents would have been double-checking by the laboratory by dawn.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence. 
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The laboratory will have double-checked the reagents by dawn." 
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the reagents" at the beginning. 
 
• Change the active verb form "will have double-checked" to "will have been double-checked" (future perfect passive). 
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the laboratory." 
 
• Ensure the time phrase "by dawn" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**. 
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The reagents will have been double-checked by the laboratory by dawn."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 
 
 
• **Option 1: **"The reagents have been double-checked by the laboratory by dawn." – Incorrect tense (present perfect passive). 
 
• **Option 3: **"The reagents will be double-checked by the laboratory by dawn." – Incorrect tense (future simple passive). 
 
• **Option 4: **"The reagents would have been double-checking by the laboratory by dawn." – Incorrect and awkward tense structure. 
</ul

questions.question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

I suggested that he **goes to the doctor immediately.**

options.text: should have go to the doctor

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**go to the doctor immediately**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The sentence is in the subjunctive mood, which is used to express suggestions, demands, or hypothetical situations.
 
• The correct structure for the subjunctive mood is "suggested that he **go**", where the base form of the verb "go" is used without adding "-s" or "-es" even for third-person singular subjects.
 
• **Option 1** uses incorrect phrasing ("go to doctor at once" is missing the article "the" before "doctor").
 
• **Option 2** ("should goes to the doctor") is grammatically incorrect because "goes" cannot follow "should."
 
• **Option 4** ("should have go to the doctor") is incorrect because the proper form would be "should have gone."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"I suggested that he **go to the doctor immediately**__."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "go to doctor at once" is incorrect because it omits the article "the" before "doctor."
 
• **Option 2:** "should goes to the doctor" is grammatically incorrect as "should" is followed by the base form of the verb.
 
• **Option 4:** "should have go to the doctor" is incorrect because the correct construction would be "should have gone to the doctor."
</ul

questions.question:
**A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.**

She said, "He doesn't listen to me."

options.text: She said he don't listen to her.
She said that he doesn't listened to her.
She said that he didn't listen to her.
She said that he didn't listened to her.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She said that he didn’t listen to her.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Direct to Indirect:**
 
 
• The verb "doesn't" in the direct speech is converted to "didn't" to match the past tense as the reporting verb "said" is in the past tense.
 
• The pronoun "me" is changed to "her" to match the subject "She" in the reporting clause.
 
 
 
• **Conjugation:**
